text:
Maya: TL;DR: we need a concise GA acceptance bundle for the Dedicated pilot called "Foundation / Plus / Platinum" tiers. Focus areas: SLA metrics, minimum public + internal docs, support/oncall handoff, monitoring deliverables (synthetics/alerts/dashboards), and pricing model for committed vs burst. Can we lock owners + deadlines now?
Alex: I like the new naming. Quick q: do tiers apply per-customer or per-endpoint? Customers asked about mixing tiers per-model.
Jordan: We can support per-endpoint tiers later. For GA, recommend per-customer tiering to keep rollout simple. Proposed SLOs (inference p95/p99, availability):

```
Foundation: p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 950ms, availability 99.4%, error-rate <1.2%
Plus:       p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 600ms, availability 99.9%, error-rate <0.6%
Platinum:   p95 <= 100ms, p99 <= 300ms, availability 99.97%, error-rate <0.15%
```

Jordan: Add synthetic checks: cold model runner (every 5m), warm runner (every 1m) and a daily throughput spike test.
Priya: Support definitions we need: incident vs ticket taxonomy, first-touch triage owner, and what escalation looks like by tier. Proposed first-touch: Platform detects & tries auto-remediation -> triage by Platform L1; if human handoff required follow the tier matrix. I'll post a rota by EOD.
Sam: Sales note: Platinum customers want named CS, guaranteed onboarding sessions, and a dedicated slack channel. They also asked if credits are available for SLA misses. Keep me in the loop before we show pricing.
Ravi (Finance): Cost delta: Plus adds ~12-18% on infra + ops, Platinum adds ~28-38% because of reserved capacity and 24/7 staffing. Credits proposal: Foundation cap 5%, Plus cap 12%, Platinum cap 30% of monthly invoice for severe downtime events. Legal sign-off required.
Elena: Docs split: Public (SLA summary card, short onboarding expectations, pricing matrix, quick FAQ). Internal (runbooks: escalation, throttling/quantized-fallback guide, dashboard runbook + how to interpret synthetics). I can draft the public pages once SLOs + fallback text are finalized.
Alex: Rollout policy: default to Plus for pilot customers, allow opt-in to Platinum if they commit capacity and term. Foundation will be for small customers or early access trials. We'll gate enforcement with a flag for 14 days after rollout.
Jordan: Fallback behavior: if Platinum reserved capacity is exhausted, route traffic to a quantized variant with header x-rw-sla=degraded and return code 200 with a `warning` field in response payload. We'll document exact latency change in fallback spec. Need product + runtime to agree on variant list.
Priya: Escalation matrix (sketch):
- Foundation: Platform L2 -> Product oncall -> CS (business hours)
- Plus: Platform L1 -> Product L1 -> CS (extended hours)
- Platinum: Platform L1 + named CS -> 24/7 escalation chain
Priya: Will add names & rotations in my follow-up.
Maya: Owners (+ due dates):
- Jordan: finalize SLO table, synthetic job names, fallback spec & dashboard templates. Due: 48h.
- Elena: public SLA page, pricing matrix draft, and FAQ outline. Due: 72h.
- Priya: oncall rotation + incident taxonomy + triage matrix. Due: EOD today.
- Alex: rollout policy doc, feature-flag plan, and API header contract for degraded responses. Due: 72h.
- Ravi: pricing delta, credit caps, and 3-term (monthly/12mo/24mo) margin sims. Due: 72h.
- Sam: GTM one-pager and a customer Q&A list (mixing tiers, per-model rules). Due: 72h.
- Maya: assemble acceptance checklist and publish. Due: 96h.
Sam: Important: customers already asked whether they can assign Platinum to only text-generation models and Foundation to embeddings. We should state GA position (no mixing) or plan to support mixing later.
Alex: For GA let's be conservative: no mixing across models per-customer. We'll add per-endpoint tiering in a later release. State that clearly in GTM.
Elena: Public SLA wording needs to be tight about credits, Force Majeure, and what counts as measurement windows. Legal wants precise language. Can Legal review a short draft by tomorrow morning?
Legal: Yes, submit the draft to legal-review channel. We'll prioritize SLA + credits language; include measurement methodology.
Ravi (Finance): For pricing bands propose: list price (no commit), 12mo (-10%), 24mo (-18%) for Plus; Platinum list with 12mo (-8%) and 24mo (-15%) — run sims for both optimistic and conservative utilization.
Jordan: Alerts: add high-seat usage alert (capacity approaching reserve) and degraded-fallback alert (when we route >5% traffic to degraded variant). Also an automated Page if degraded routing persists >5m for Platinum customers.
DeployBot: [info] Dashboard template "foundation-plus-sla-template-v1" created by Jordan (https://dashboards.redwood/sla/foundation-plus-v1)
Priya: Blocker: need a clear decision on whether Platform will own first-touch for all generated-content incidents. If Product owns some categories we need to adjust rotations.
Maya: Decision: Platform owns detection & first-touch for all infra/perf incidents; Product owns functional/regression incidents (prompt quality, hallucination) once triaged by Platform. Priya, incorporate this into triage matrix.
Alex: I'll add the feature-flag and a rollout experiment to measure enforcement-quality for 2 weeks. We'll log metrics: fraction of requests hitting reserved pool, tail latencies, and fallback rate.
Sam: GTM ask: create a short buyer-facing chart showing tradeoffs (latency/uptime/cost/response-time). I can draft if Elena gives me the SLO numbers.
Maya: Any other blockers?
Elena: We need to confirm the sample measurement windows (monthly window definition) so the SLA page has an unambiguous meter.
Legal: We'll standardize on UTC calendar month and publish the measurement methodology.
Maya: OK. I'll consolidate these action owners into a short acceptance checklist and post back after Priya's rota. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
